diagram_math_checks.objects: t-plane with cut (-infinity,0], principal power t^{-z}=exp(-z Log t), x>0 on t=-x, small radius r.
diagram_math_checks.justification: def-hankel-contour-and-power-branch defines the principal branch with -pi<arg t<pi; theorem Statement and proof step 2.1 use these same objects.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Lower boundary arg t approaches -pi, hence t^{-z} approaches exp(pi i z)x^{-z}; upper boundary arg t approaches pi, hence t^{-z} approaches exp(-pi i z)x^{-z}.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Substitution into the supplier principal-power definition agrees exactly with the boundary-value formula in proof step 2.1 and the two drawn labels.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Lower segment points right toward zero; upper segment points left away from zero. Arc angles increase from -150 degrees through 0 to 150 degrees, giving the counterclockwise detour.
diagram_math_checks.justification: These arrows implement supplier L3 lower-inward/counterclockwise/upper-outward order. Rays are vertically separated and near-cut arc endpoints stylized as explicitly explained; no exact boundary parametrization is asserted.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Lower ray has decreasing x and dt=-dx, yielding a positive integral over x from 0 to infinity; upper ray has increasing x and dt=-dx, yielding its negative.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Direct change of variables t=-x recovers exactly exp(pi i z) minus exp(-pi i z) in proof step 2.1.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The dashed cut is not contour; radius-r detour contribution vanishes for 0<Re z<1.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The branch domain excludes the cut; proof step 1.1 bounds the circular integrand by O(r^{-Re z}) and the arc length is O(r), giving O(r^{1-Re z}). All three existing proof steps are byte-preserved and do not depend on the figure.
